toml:
# Quantum preset: a cold-atom interferometer (CAI) accelerometer, built from its
# interferometer physics, against a navigation-grade quartz accelerometer during a GNSS
# outage. A one-dimensional dead-reckoning coast: 10 minutes of GNSS, then 110 minutes
# denied.
#
# The quantum sensor carries an [accel_quantum.cai] table, so its velocity-random-walk
# floor q_va is DERIVED from the interferometer: k_eff = 4*pi/lambda, projection noise
# 1/(C*sqrt(N)) per shot, the cycle time, and a stated platform vibration level added in
# quadrature (docs/QUANTUM.md). The supplied q_va is only the fallback if the table is
# removed. The residual bias is the published bias stability of a laboratory hybrid quantum
# accelerometer. The interferometer parameters are a bracket in the published range, not a
# datasheet of any instrument.
#
# What it answers: how long each sensor keeps the dead-reckoned position inside 100 m, and
# how the position error grows, when one sensor is specified by interferometer physics and
# the other by a datasheet. MODELLED: a single-axis error model, not a three-axis
# navigation solution, and no statement about any real instrument. The further CAI error
# terms (laser-phase noise, wavefront curvature, fringe ambiguity) are library functions,
# not yet part of this kind.
kind = "inertial"
seed = 20261013
threshold_m = 100.0

[time]
step_s = 10.0
duration_s = 7200.0

[gnss]
windows = [
  { t0 = 0.0,   t1 = 600.0,  state = "nominal" },
  { t0 = 600.0, t1 = 7200.0, state = "denied" },
]

[accel_quantum]
id = "cold-atom-interferometer"
provenance = "Cold-atom (Rb-87 D2) interferometric accelerometer: q_va derived from the [accel_quantum.cai] parameters, a bracket in the GAIN/MAIUS literature range (Freier et al. arXiv:1512.05660; Becker et al. Nature 2018); residual bias 5.88e-7 m/s^2 = the 6e-8 g bias stability of a laboratory hybrid quantum accelerometer (Templier et al., Science Advances 2022, arXiv:2209.13209). Laboratory maturity, not deployed."
bias = 5.88e-7
q_va = 4.6656e-8   # fallback only: overridden by the interferometer physics below

[accel_quantum.cai]
wavelength_m = 780.241209e-9   # Rb-87 D2 line
pulse_sep_t = 0.02             # pulse separation T (s)
atom_number = 1.0e6            # detected atoms per shot N
contrast = 0.5                 # initial fringe contrast C0
cycle_time_s = 0.5             # measurement cycle time T_c (s)
vibration_psd = 1.0e-12        # stated platform vibration PSD (m/s^2)^2/Hz along the axis

[accel_classical]
id = "nav-grade-quartz"
provenance = "Navigation-grade quartz accelerometer (Honeywell QA-2000 / Groves AESS Tutorial): bias stability ~160 ug = 1.57e-3 m/s^2; noise ~20 ug/sqrtHz = 1.96e-4 (m/s^2)/sqrtHz; bias instability ~1 ug = 1e-5 m/s^2; modest acceleration random walk"
bias = 1.57e-3
q_va = 3.8416e-8
bias_instability = 1.0e-5
q_aa = 1.0e-13
summary: scenario f89a927e605a | quantum holdover 6600s p95 9.85m | classical holdover 350s p95 30641.5m
